I am pleased to present the Uganda Railways Corporation (URC) Budget Estimates for the Financial Year 2026/27, which outline our strategic priorities, resource allocations, and planned interventions aimed at accelerating railway development and enhancing national logistics efficiency. This budget has been developed through a consultative process involving key stakeholders, including the Ministry of Works and Transport (MoWT), MoFPED, the private sector, and development partners, to ensure shared understanding and alignment on the critical issues affecting the Corporation and the appropriate measures to address them.

The FY 2026/27 Budget is aligned with the national Budget theme: “Full Monetization of Uganda’s Economy through Commercial Agriculture, Industrialization, Expanding and Broadening Services, Digital Transformation, and Market Access.” In line with this, URC’s planned investments are focused on lowering the cost of transport, improving rail connectivity to key industrial and agricultural production zones, and facilitating efficient regional trade. Priority interventions will include the rehabilitation of strategic rail corridors, acquisition and maintenance of rolling stock, expansion of port and intermodal facilities, and strengthening of digital systems to enhance operational efficiency.

The FY 2026/27 budget is projected to significantly improve performance across key indicators. Freight volumes are expected to increase from 314,434 metric tonnes in FY 2025/26 to 487,000 metric tonnes in FY 2026/27, while passenger numbers are projected to rise from 550,000 to 1,088,780 over the same period. Revenue performance is also anticipated to grow from UGX 29.01 billion to UGX 44.59 billion, reflecting improved operational efficiency and service delivery. These outcomes will contribute to enhanced national competitiveness through more efficient and cost-effective transport logistics.

URC remains committed to upholding fiscal discipline, ensuring value for money, and maintaining transparency in financial management and reporting. We will continue to work closely with the Government of Uganda, development partners, and the private sector to deliver measurable results in line with the Fourth National Development Plan (NDP IV).

On behalf of the Corporation, I wound like to commend the deliberate Government effort to have the railway sector completely revitalised as exhibited in the supplementary budget offered in the financial year 2025/26 and the increasing of Government subvention to 110Bn in the financial year 2026/27

I wish to express my sincere appreciation to the Board of Directors, the Government of Uganda, and the dedicated URC staff for their continued guidance and commitment to restoring rail transport as a cornerstone of Uganda’s economic transformation.
Together, we shall continue to rebuild a modern, efficient, and sustainable railway system that supports Uganda’s journey towards full economic monetization and regional integration.
I hereby submit the URC Budget Estimates amounting to UGX 346.28 billion for FY 2026/27 for your approval.

This Executive Summary presents the Uganda Railways Corporation (URC) Budget for the Financial Year 2026/27. The budget outlines the Corporation’s planned revenues, expenditures, and key interventions aimed at enhancing railway infrastructure, operational efficiency, and service delivery. It aligns with the national theme for FY 2026/27, “Full
Monetization of Uganda’s Economy through Commercial Agriculture, Industrialization, Expanding and Broadening Services, Digital Transformation and Market Access.”

The FY 2026/27 Budget is anchored on the URC Strategic Plan, the Business Turnaround Strategy, and the National Development Plan (NDP IV) priorities on transport infrastructure and logistics modernization. As highlighted above, URC’s focus for the financial year will be on strengthening its operational capacity and improving the reliability of the national railway network through targeted interventions in infrastructure, rolling stock, and digital transformation.
The key Priorities for this budget include but not limited to the following:

Infrastructure Rehabilitation and Modernization: Completion of ongoing works on Tororo–Gulu lines, alongside the rehabilitation of the Kampala–Malaba, Kampala-Kyengera-Bujjuko and Kampala-Port Bell–Jinja corridor under the AfDB to boost regional and port connectivity.
Rolling Stock Acquisition and Maintenance: Procurement and overhaul of locomotives, wagons, and passenger coaches to increase service reliability and capacity.

Operational Efficiency and Safety: Investment in track maintenance equipment, signalling systems, and staff capacity building to ensure safety and timely service delivery. Others include: Development of a Railway Transport Master Plan, Development of a Railway Transport Policy, Operationalization of Tororo-Gulu railway line and Monitoring and Evaluation of budget performance

Digital Transformation: Deployment of ICT-based railway management systems for ticketing, asset tracking, and operational monitoring such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system and an Automated Train Warning (ATW) System.

Revenue Mobilization and Partnerships: Strengthening public–private partnerships (PPPs) to mobilize investment and diversify revenue streams. This will be conducted in reference and alignment to the Revenue Mobilisation Strategy.
Intermodal and Port Development: Enhancement of Port Bell and Jinja piers to support multimodal freight operations in collaboration with Lake Victoria transport operators.

Considering the period ranging from 1st July 2025 to 31st March 2026, the Corporation realised revenue worth 10,562,799 and 5,853,177 accruing from internally generated revenue and grants from Government of Uganda Respectively totalling16,415,976 while the total operating expense stood at 54,906,021 implying an operating loss of 38,490,045. The high operating loss is attributed to rising cost of depreciation 30,189,343 accounting for 55% of the total operating expense.

Uganda Railways Corporation (URC) is a corporate body established by the Uganda Railways Corporation Act (1992) Cap 216. The mandate of the Corporation is: the construction, operation and maintenance of railway, marine and road services both in and outside Uganda, for the carriage of passengers and goods.
The Preferred Freight and Passenger Transporter in Eastern Africa
To provide reliable Railway & Marine Services for Social-Economic Transformation

The following core values support the vision and mission of the corporation. They underpin its operations, the behaviour of its staff and guide the implementation of its strategic plans: Accountability, Integrity, Teamwork, Reliability, Innovation, Efficiency, Safety and Customer care.

The Uganda Railways Corporation (URC) Budget 2026/27FY has been prepared based on Integrated Transport Infrastructure and Services Programme (ITIS) and URC priority interventions in the Five-Year Strategic Plan, NDPIV Programme Implementation Action Plans (PIAPs), the Budget Call Circular 2026-27, the NRM Manifesto (2026-2031) and the provisions in section 9 of the Public Finance and Management Act 2015. The preparation of this budget has been guided fully by the URC Management and Board from allocation of resources up to identification of priority areas to focus on during FY 2026-27. The process of the Budget preparation was so consultative that all departments and sections were actively involved. This Budget presents information relating to all departments with the resource envelope worth UGX 346.28Bn

This FY 2026/27 seeks to achieve the URC Strategic Objectives as clearly highlighted in the five-year 2025/26-2029/30 Strategic Plan of the Corporation through the attainment of the key outputs and outcomes prioritized in the departmental work plans. These strategic objectives include;
To develop sustainable railway transport infrastructure and services in the country;
To strengthen railway transport assets management;
To improve the Corporation’s competitiveness and efficiency in the management of rail and marine transport services; and
To strengthen the institutional capacity of the Corporation.
The Corporation majorly aims at adopting a Budget Strategy which will enhance the successful implementation of the forthcoming FY Budget which includes but not limited to;
Charging of market rates above the cost of doing business,
Fast-track valuation of rental property and invoicing at market rates, advertising income from advertising on assets, e.g., coaches, stations, locomotives and wagons
The 2026/27 FY Budget for URC will be guided by some of the relevant Government
National Focus Areas that may include but not limited to:
Facilitating economic growth and competitiveness by increasing investments in the real economy to maximize returns from public infrastructure;
Consolidating infrastructure development to reduce the cost of doing business iii. Digital transformation
As a strategic public enterprise, Uganda Railways Corporation is a critical enabler of monetization through transport infrastructure, logistics efficiency, and regional trade facilitation.

The Budget Estimates for FY 2026/27 outline the Uganda Railways Corporation’s (URC) projected resource envelope worth UGX 346.28Bn to support its operational, maintenance, and strategic development priorities. The estimates reflect Government’s continued commitment to revitalising the railway subsector, alongside URC’s efforts to enhance internally generated revenues and improve operational efficiency. The budget is structured to balance recurrent obligations with ongoing infrastructure rehabilitation and development interventions, particularly along key corridors such as the Tororo–Gulu line.
Table  SEQ Table \* ARABIC 2: Approved Budget Estimates for FY 2026/27

The total projected budget for FY 2026/27 amounts to UGX 346.283 billion of which 39% will be obtained from GOU-Ext-African Development bank, and 48% from Government support in form of subvention and counterpart funding while only 13% is expected from Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) indicating how the corporation is overly dependent on Government and external support. However, efforts, policies and strategies are in place to minimise the extent of Corporation dependence and even attain self sustainability in the few years possible.

The projected expenditure (UGX 346.283Bn) will be disaggregated by wage, non-wage and Development expenditure. Wage expenditure will mainly cover Contract Staff Salaries and Allowances, Casuals, Temporary Staff wages and Allowances, Allowances for Seconded Staff, URC NSSF Contributions, and Gratuity Expenses worth UGX 22.991bn. Non-wage expenditure comprising of Medical Expenses (To Employees), Retrenchment Costs, Advertising Workshops and Seminars, Staff Training, Recruitment Expenses, Tender Adverts, Staff Welfare among others accounting for UGX 60.523bn while development expenditure constituting of Land acquisition, residential and non-residential buildings renovations, Permanent Way rehabilitation, Station, Yards/Sidings, Bridges & Culverts maintenance, rolling stock acquisition, Furniture And Fittings, Office Equipment, Motor Vehicles, Machinery and other equipment will constitute UGX 262.768bn as summarised in the table below:

Overall, the budget reflects sustained national efforts toward modernisation, rehabilitation, and improved competitiveness of rail transport in Uganda.

The total budget of FY 2026/27 departmental allocation is UGX 345.88Bn with Mechanical Engineering having the highest budget 55.57% because of the need to address the ever-increasing demand for new rollingstock and the respective maintenance, followed by Civil Engineering budget with 23.01% allocation, Human Resource department at 11.55% due to staff and fixed cost including operationalisation of Tororo-Gulu line. Other remaining departments perform the supportive role and have therefore been allocated relatively below 5% justifying the strategic importance of the above three departments respectively,

This FY Budget estimates will address issues of Gender and Equity in form of offering equal emolument opportunities to all gender categories impartially. It will also focus on climate change issues by integrating greening initiatives in railway transport infrastructure development, waste and disposal management plans in place. Environment certification for the marine vessels in place before their operation. Additionally, traffic signals will be installed at level crossings for MGR rehabilitation projects to ensure safety of all users of Transport services.

On HIV/Aids, there will be sensitization of staffs on HIV/AIDS HIV/AIDS preventive measures implemented at project areas; and implementation of HIV/AIDS workplace policy. Finally, medical insurance will be expanded in scope to cover HIV/AIDS associated treatments.

On Human rights issues, the corporation plans and implements decent work environment with healthy breaks and overtime compensations. The corporation recognizes Workers union and staff are free to subscribe to them.
